name: Godspeed You! Black Emperor
label: Constellation
lede: A Montreal collective with no singer, no frontman and no interest in your approval made hour-long records about the end of the world, got held by police at an Oklahoma gas station, and called a prize gala they'd just won insane.

eras.title: A biker film, a loft and five hundred envelopes
eras.text: Godspeed started as three people in Montreal and grew into a shifting crowd of guitars, strings and tape. Their first real record was pressed in a run of 500 and hand-assembled by the band, which is about as far from a music industry as you can get.

years.h: Efrim Menuck, Mike Moya and Mauro Pezzente start a band
years.p: The three form Godspeed You! Black Emperor in Montreal, first put together as a support act for local band Steak 72. The name comes from Mitsuo Yanagimachi's 1976 Japanese documentary about the Black Emperors biker gang.

years.h: The first cassette: All Lights Fucked on the Hairy Amp Drooling
years.p: Efrim Menuck makes a tiny-run cassette with help from Mauro Pezzente. For almost three decades it's the most hunted-after object in the band's world.
years.xp: The tape stayed mostly theoretical for fans until February 2022, when a copy surfaced on 4chan's /mu/ board. On February 14, 2022 the band put the full audio up on its own Bandcamp.

years.src: Wikipedia: F♯ A♯ ∞ · Wikipedia: Efrim Menuck
years.h: Recording F♯ A♯ ∞ at Hotel2Tango, Mile End
years.p: Godspeed records its debut in May 1997 at Hotel2Tango, a Mile End loft that had been Gallery Quiva. Efrim Menuck had set the room up as a studio around 1996.

years.cap: Godspeed You! Black Emperor · via Discogs
years.h: F♯ A♯ ∞ LP · 500 copies, each with a train-crushed penny
years.p: Constellation releases the LP as CST003, hand-packaged and numbered. Each jacket has one of three photos glued on by hand, and the envelope inside holds a handbill, a Menuck drawing and a Canadian penny flattened by a train.
years.xp:
The jackets were made by the band, the label and Montreal artists, with a watertower, a train or a road sign photo stuck on each. A silk-screened image honors blues musician Reverend Gary Davis. The vinyl ends in a locked groove, which is why the running time is written as infinity.

The spoken opening of "The Dead Flag Blues" came from an unfinished screenplay by Efrim Menuck. Later pressings swap in a US penny, since Canada stopped minting them.

eras.title: Kranky takes the tapes south
eras.text: The band mailed their LP to Chicago's Kranky hoping for help touring the States, and Kranky put it out on CD. Over the next four years a nine-piece Godspeed became the reference point for what orchestral post-rock sounded like, and the band's politics got louder with every sleeve.

years.h: Kranky reissues F♯ A♯ ∞ on CD with an extra half hour
years.p: The band sent the LP to Kranky hoping to tour the US. Kranky's CD, krank 027, runs 63 minutes against the LP's 38, with reworked sections and new material, and lands fourth in The Wire's 1998 critics' poll.

years.h: Mike Moya leaves for HṚṢṬA; Roger Tellier-Craig steps in
years.p: Mike Moya exits to focus on HṚṢṬA and Roger Tellier-Craig of [[Fly Pan Am|c191214c-31e6-4d26-bfa7-35be4d90d178]] takes his guitar. The band settles into a nine-piece and starts touring.

years.cap: Hebrew on the front, Italian on the back
years.src: Wikipedia: Slow Riot for New Zerø Kanada
years.h: Slow Riot for New Zerø Kanada: a Molotov diagram on the back
years.p: The two-track EP never names the band on its outer packaging. The front reads Tohu VaVohu in Hebrew, the case opens backwards, and the back carries Italian instructions for making a Molotov cocktail.
years.xp: "Moya" is named for Mike Moya and reworks a Górecki symphony. "BBF3" is built around a street interview with a man calling himself Blaise Bailey Finnegan III, whose poem borrows from Iron Maiden. Dale Morningstar recorded it at The Gas Station in Toronto.

years.h: Lift Your Skinny Fists: four 20-minute pieces cut in nine days
years.p: Recorded at Chemical Sound in Toronto in February 2000 with Daryl Smith, from material the band had been playing live. Constellation's vinyl comes October 9, Kranky's CD October 23.
years.xp: The Village Voice called it the best movie it had seen all year. Pitchfork put it fifth for 2000 and 65th for the decade.
play: Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven

years.h: Yanqui U.X.O.: Steve Albini, and a war chart on the back
years.p: The third album is recorded in Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The back cover maps major record labels' ties to the military-industrial complex, and the liner notes tie "09-15-00" to Ariel Sharon's march on al-Haram al-Sharif.

q: The whole film was cut to Godspeed in my head.
years.h: Danny Boyle cuts 28 Days Later to Godspeed
years.p: An edit of "The Sad Mafioso" from F♯ A♯ ∞ plays in Danny Boyle's zombie film. Boyle said the whole film ran on Godspeed in his head.
years.xp: Boyle said the soundtrack to 28 Days Later was Godspeed, full stop. For a lot of people, it was the first time they heard the band.

eras.title: Held at a gas station in Ardmore
eras.text: On tour in the States, the band's appearance and Canadian plates were enough for a gas station attendant to call in terrorism. A few months later Godspeed went quiet for seven years.

years.big: Ardmore, Oklahoma: held until the FBI arrived
q: It's a good thing we're nice white kids from Canada.
years.h: Police and the FBI hold Godspeed in Ardmore, Oklahoma
years.p: A gas station attendant decides the band look like terrorists. Police detain them until FBI agents question them, find anti-government papers and oil-rig photos, and let them go after background checks.
years.xp: Nothing incriminating turned up. At the next show in St. Louis, Efrim Menuck made the point about who gets let go. Michael Moore wrote the incident into his book Dude, Where's My Country?

years.h: Constellation announces a hiatus "for the better part of a year"
years.p: Constellation says Godspeed will rest while members work on other bands. The break lasts seven years, filled by Thee Silver Mt. Zion Memorial Orchestra, [[Fly Pan Am|c191214c-31e6-4d26-bfa7-35be4d90d178]], HṚṢṬA, Esmerine and Set Fire to Flames.

eras.title: God's pee rolls again
eras.text: The reunion came with a joke and without apologies, and the second life has been busier than the first: new records, first trips to China and Australia, a Polaris Prize, and a public fight with the gala that handed it to them.

years.cap: Godspeed You! Black Emperor · via Discogs
years.h: Godspeed announces a reunion for All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: The statement says god's pee has decided to roll again. Mike Moya comes back; cellist Norsola Johnson declines. A full North American and European tour follows in 2011.

years.h: 'Allelujah! Don't Bend! Ascend!, first album in ten years
years.p: Timothy Herzog replaces drummer Bruce Cawdron. The year also brings Coachella and Pitchfork Music Festival, stages the old Godspeed would never have played.

years.big: Toyota paid for the party. Godspeed said so.
years.h: Godspeed wins the Polaris Prize and trashes the gala
years.p: Accepting the Polaris for 'Allelujah!, the band's statement calls a Toyota-sponsored gala in a time of austerity insane and tone-deaf. They suggest the next one happen in a cruddier hall.
years.xp:
The band said they'd put the prize money toward musical instruments for people in Quebec prisons.

That fall they also opened for [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]] on the Tension tour and played Australia, New Zealand and China for the first time.

years.h: Asunder, Sweet and Other Distress after years of touring
years.p: The fifth album arrives in the middle of heavy world touring. On the road the band previews new pieces fans nickname "Buildings" and "Railroads" after the projections behind them.

years.h: Luciferian Towers · sixth album
years.p: Godspeed's sixth record, released on Constellation, keeps the reunion pace of one album every couple of years.

eras.title: Every record a statement
eras.text: Efrim Menuck calls himself an anarchist and the band's recent titles make their politics impossible to miss. In 2025 they pulled their music off Spotify rather than share a platform with a military AI investment.

years.h: G_d's Pee at State's End!
years.p: The seventh album. The same year the band joins more than 600 musicians pledging to boycott Israel until the occupation of Palestinian territories ends.

years.h: Three untitled new songs at the Knockdown Center, New York
years.p: Godspeed debuts new material in Queens, six months before announcing the album it becomes.

years.h: An album titled with the Gaza death toll
years.p: No Title as of 13 February 2024 28,340 Dead takes its name from the Palestinian death count in Gaza on the day it was conceived. The band tours ten countries behind it.
play: No Title as of 13 February 2024 28,340 Dead

years.h: Godspeed pulls its catalog from Spotify over Helsing
years.p: The band removes nearly all its music from Spotify, Tidal and Deezer, objecting to Daniel Ek's Prima Materia fund backing military AI company Helsing. Bandcamp stays up.

years.h: First South American show announced, in Brazil
years.p: Thirty-two years in, Godspeed books its first South American date.
